title: Staged deprecation and backcompat rollout notes
content:
Purpose:

This is my personal scratchpad for the staged deprecation and backward-compatibility rollout strategy for the upcoming change to the streaming tokenizer semantics (v2) and the related default KV cache eviction behavior. Goal: minimize customer-visible regressions while allowing us to flip the new default for Hosted API and Dedicated fleets within a controlled window.

High-level constraints / context:
- Change touches both runtime and SDK behavior (server-side change + minor client negotiation header).
- Some long-lived embeddings/LLM sessions rely on old KV eviction semantics; risk of latent tokenization drift in a subset of clients.
- We must support Private deployments (on-prem/VPC) where customers may not upgrade; ensure graceful negotiation and explicit opt-in/opt-out.
- Timeline: warmup + canary mid-Feb, progressive ramp through Mar with final default change by end of Q1.

Rollout components (what we control):
1) Server-side flag: tokenizer-v2-enabled: false|true|auto. 
   - false: old behavior (current default)
   - true: new behavior enforced unconditionally
   - auto: server negotiates with SDK header, can act as safe bridge (returns compatibility metadata)
2) SDK header: X-RW-Tokenizer-Version: v1|v2|auto. SDKs publish auto by default in next release (auto -> prefer v2, but fallback if server indicates known incompatibility).
3) Pinning API: existing route-level pinning stays; add model-compat pin label to routes so clients can pin to runtime with tokenizer-v1.
4) Rollout policy: cohort-based (client affinity + route affinity).

Suggested staged plan (concrete):
- Preflight (Feb 10–17):
  - Deploy server builds with tokenizer-v2 feature flag behind runtime config; enable telemetry hooks.
  - Cut SDK prerelease with header support (X-RW-Tokenizer-Version) -> test internally.
  - Add a canary-specific dashboard: tokenization-diff, avg-perplexity-change, failed-inference-rate, session-reset-rate.
  - Notify major customers whose integrations we think are at risk (list maintained in Confluence).

- Canary 1 (Feb 18–24): lightweight internal canary
  - Route 0.5% of traffic (internal product & opt-in test orgs) to tokenizer-v2:true with SDK header=v2.
  - Monitor signal windows: 5m/1h/24h. Watch for climb in errors (>1.5x baseline), perplexity regressions (>2.5% median shift), latency tail change.
  - Quick pivot path: immediately flip tokenizer-v2 back to auto for the cohort; roll forward fixes as needed.

- Canary 2 (Mar 1–7): public canary, narrow customer cohorts
  - 1–3% traffic split; include some external early-adopter customers that signed up.
  - Enable KV-eviction-telemetry keyed by customer id + model id (sampled 1/20 to limit overhead).
  - Run A/B internal evals: sample identical prompts across v1/v2 to detect output drift on key prompt-sets.
  - Collection: save first 128 tokens and metadata for diffs (PII scrub rules apply).

- Ramp (Mar 8–24): progressive increases 5% -> 25% -> 50%
  - At each step require sign-off from oncall, release-owner, and product-ops.
  - Ramp rules: no persistent signal breach in previous 24h (see thresholds below).
  - Open opt-in for customers via Console toggle and API route pin (model-compat pin).

- Default flip / postfix (Mar 25–31):
  - If ramp stable, flip Hosted API default to auto (with server-side preference for v2), but keep dedicated and private unaffected unless they opt-in or schedule upgrade.
  - Post-change: maintain a compatibility-mode API endpoint for 90 days where customers can request enforced v1 behavior for a named route.

Risk matrix and mitigation ideas:
- Risk: Silent semantic drift in long-running chats 
  - Mitigation: detect session-reset-rate and KL divergence between prefix token distributions; if exceed thresholds, force cohort fallback to v1 and notify customers immediately.
- Risk: On-prem customers unable to upgrade SDK -> mismatch
  - Mitigation: server-side auto mode will prefer v1 for older agent-user-agents (server tracks sdk-version header). Rollout docs to customers + one-off patch packages.
- Risk: Cost/latency regression for certain model families with tokenizer-v2 
  - Mitigation: keep per-model kernel selection pinned; use smart routing to fall back to compatible model variant with cached quantization profile.

Signal thresholds (early-warning):
- error-rate: +100% over baseline for 1h -> immediate abort for cohort
- median-perplexity (evaluated on eval prompt set): >3% shift for 24h -> pause ramp
- session-reset-rate: +50% persistent over 6h -> rollback cohort
- tail-latency (p99): +20% sustained for 2h -> investigate, consider rollback
- downstream customer escalations: any P0 outage reported by a customer in cohort -> immediate rollback and incident call

Operational notes / playbook snippets:
- Before touching the flags, create a release label in Console and pin a snapshot of route configs (so rollback is reversible).
- Channeling: #runtime-release-discuss for async updates; paging via #oncall-runtime for P1s.
- Telemetry owners: Arjun for runtime metrics, Maya for evaluation suite, Leo for customer comms.
- Debug dumps: sampling at 1/100 of requests for full payloads. Ensure we TTL dumps and scrub keys.

Quick checklist (pre-deploy):
- [ ] SDK prerelease published and smoke-tested (mac/py/js)
- [ ] Server builds with tokenizer-v2 behind config deployed to canary stack
- [ ] Console toggle UI wired to route-level pinning
- [ ] Canaries dashboard created + grafana alerts configured (thresholds above)
- [ ] Customer advisory email draft ready and reviewed by legal (Maya)
- [ ] Ops runbook created with rollback commands and re-pinning steps
- [ ] Ensure backups of model cache and prefix caches (where applicable)

Notes-to-self / unanswered questions:
- Do we want to make auto behavior prefer server-declared compatibility matrix per route rather than purely SDK-header driven? Pros: finer control for Private. Cons: more complexity in negotiation.
- How to handle third-party proxies that strip custom headers? Need header fallback via initial negotiation handshake (first request/response exchange) and store in session metadata.
- Is the 90-day compatibility endpoint policy acceptable to legal? Follow up with Privacy & Legal.

Customer comms snippet (for email / Console banner):
"We are rolling out an update to our tokenizer and cache semantics that improves alignment and reduces unexpected token drift for most models. We will stage this change and provide a per-route compatibility toggle. If you rely on long-running sessions and precise token-level stability, please opt-in to the compatibility check or contact support to schedule a dedicated validation window."

Follow-ups (practical next steps I will take):
- Draft the SDK header spec and put a mini-PR for the Node/Go clients (timeline: 48h)
- Add compatibility-matrix field to model metadata in the Catalog service (small schema change, coord with Product)
- Run internal evals with 3 production prompt-sets and share diffs on Confluence (Maya owns)
- Sync with Solutions Eng to identify top 10 customers to pre-notify (Leo owns)

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally messy — will tidy for the playbook once we validate the first canary.
